title: The Letters of Sandpiper Point
premise: Theo Sterling, a ghostwriter who buries her own voice in other people's stories, is hired to pen the memoirs of rival author Julian Voss — and discovers he's the man she loved and abandoned a decade ago in Sandpiper Point. When a family reunion forces Theo to produce a date, Julian agrees to play the part, and the fake courtship rekindles everything they never said. As the memoir deadline looms, Theo must decide whether to confess her authorship and her betrayal, knowing the book's publication will expose both. In the end, she chooses honesty over the contract, Julian publishes the memoir under both their names, and they return to Sandpiper Point not to repeat the past but to write a new first chapter together.
about_author: Felix Hartwell is the pseudonym of a former ghostwriter who spent twelve years lending her voice to other people's love stories before claiming one of her own. She writes from a rented cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she insists the tide keeps better deadlines than any editor.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In her Brooklyn apartment, Theo finishes ghostwriting a bestselling romance and receives a lucrative, anonymous offer to write a rival author's memoir. She accepts out of financial desperation, hiding the contract from her agent. Emotional beat: the ache of erasure — she's fluent in everyone's voice but her own.

chapters.title: Summons to Sandpiper Point
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Her grandmother's estate summons the whole family to a reunion at Sandpiper Point, the coastal town where Theo grew up and where she once broke a young man's heart by leaving without a word. Her mother demands she bring a serious partner. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Rival's Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the first memoir meeting in a Manhattan hotel bar, the client turns out to be Julian Voss — the boy from Sandpiper Point, now a famous novelist. Neither betrays recognition in front of his publisher. Emotional beat: a held breath; the past sitting down at the table.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A flashback chapter: nineteen-year-old Theo and Julian on the Sandpiper Point dunes, the promise they made, and the morning she vanished to chase a writing fellowship. Emotional beat: tender, then gutting — the reader learns exactly what she did.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian privately confronts Theo: he knows who she is, and he'll let her write the memoir only if she agrees to be his date to his publisher's gala — and, when he learns of her reunion, hers. A pact of mutual convenience. Emotional beat: wounded pride disguising hope.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They script their fake relationship over coffee — how they met, first kiss, inside jokes — and the invented details keep colliding with real memories. Emotional beat: laughter turning dangerous, the blur between performance and truth.

chapters.title: The Reunion Begins
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Julian arrive at Sandpiper Point; her family scrutinizes, her grandmother approves instantly, and old neighbors remember Julian as the boy who waited on the dock. Emotional beat: exposure anxiety — the town itself is a witness.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At the reunion dinner, Julian defends Theo against a cutting toast from her mother, and their staged handhold becomes unscripted. On the porch afterward, they nearly kiss and retreat. Emotional beat: the fake date stops being fake.

chapters.title: Interviews and Confessions Half-Said
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Memoir sessions begin; Julian answers questions about a lost love with details only she would recognize, testing whether she'll admit it. She transcribes around the truth. Emotional beat: cat and mouse where both are prey.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian finds a weathered tin on the beach containing letters Theo wrote him at nineteen and never sent, kept by his late mother. He reads them alone. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness — proof she loved him all along.

chapters.title: The Memoir's Missing Chapter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The publisher demands the memoir's centerpiece: the love story Julian refuses to discuss. Theo realizes finishing the book means writing her own betrayal in his voice. Emotional beat: the trap closing — duty versus love made literal.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A nor'easter strands the family; Theo and Julian shelter together and finally sleep together, and in the dark he almost tells her about the letters. She almost tells him about the memoir. Neither does. Emotional beat: intimacy built on two withheld truths.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Version
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's mother reveals why she always opposed Theo's writing — a buried family story of a woman who lost everything to ambition — and demands Theo choose the safe publishing path. Emotional beat: understanding without absolution; the mirror sharpens.

chapters.title: Deadline and Discovery
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian's editor, reviewing draft pages Theo couriered, praises passages that quote the unsent letters verbatim. Julian realizes Theo has read them — or written them. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Confrontation on the Dock
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confronts Theo with the tin of letters; she confesses she wrote them and, cornered, that she is his ghostwriter. He accuses her of stealing his story twice — once by leaving, once by narrating it. Emotional beat: the breakup that was ten years late.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone in her childhood bedroom, Theo rereads her own unsent letters and drafts a resignation from the memoir, confronting the self-loathing that made her flee love and authorship alike. Emotional beat: the forgiveness she must grant herself before asking for his.

chapters.title: What Julian Decided
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian rereads the letters and the draft and recognizes that the ghostwriter's voice and the girl on the dunes were always the same person — that she gave his story back truer than he could. He drafts something of his own. Emotional beat: anger cooling into choice.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the reunion's closing night, Julian publicly reads the memoir's final chapter — crediting its true author — and asks Theo to stay, in front of everyone she spent her life performing for. Emotional beat: public vulnerability as redemption.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Cover
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo renegotiates the contract: the memoir will carry both their names, her first byline in twelve years. Her mother, watching, offers a fragile truce. Emotional beat: reclaiming identity without abandoning love.

chapters.title: The Letter She Finally Sends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo mails Julian the one unsent letter she kept back, with a new ending written in her own hand. He answers by arriving at her door with the tin and a blank notebook. Emotional beat: the past answered, not erased.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. A year later: the memoir launches at Sandpiper Point's bookshop, and Theo reads aloud under her own name while Julian watches from the back row. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — timing, finally, kept.

chapters.title: Sandpiper Point, Continued
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the dunes where they were nineteen, Theo and Julian bury the tin of letters as an offering to the tide and open the blank notebook to page one. Emotional beat: resolution — love chosen daily, a story they now write together.
